claims.text: The initial AlCoCrFeNi eutectic alloy has a continuous brittle dual-phase lamellar microstructure that is prone to catastrophic interfacial cracking and low room-temperature ductility.
Severe cold rolling followed by short high-temperature annealing will transform the AlCoCrFeNi lamellar structure into a patterned heterogeneous grain structure.
An 80% room-temperature thickness reduction is an appropriate deformation step for producing the proposed heterogeneous structure.
Annealing at 900–1000 °C for 1–5 minutes after rolling will induce partial recrystallization in AlCoCrFeNi.
An annealing window of 0.6–0.75 of the melting temperature will selectively recrystallize the softer phase while retaining the hard phase as a barrier.
The resulting structure will contain coarse grains larger than 10 μm and ultrafine grains smaller than 1 μm within lamellar bands.
The heterogeneous grain-size distribution will generate internal back stresses.
A plastic-deformation gradient between coarse and fine regions generates back-stress or hetero-deformation-induced hardening.
Back-stress hardening delays necking and thereby prolongs uniform plastic deformation.
The heterogeneous structure redistributes stress away from phase interfaces and prevents interfacial crack initiation and propagation.
A dynamically reinforced heterogeneous grain structure has prolonged ductility in a CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy.
The proposed treatment will produce uniform elongation above 15% and ultimate tensile strength above 1.5 GPa in AlCoCrFeNi.
The proposed treatment will markedly reduce interfacial crack density relative to the as-cast state.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi baseline has less than 5% ductility and fails catastrophically at phase interfaces.
Exceeding an upper annealing-temperature threshold would completely homogenize or dissolve the eutectic lamellar structure into a single-phase solid solution.
Excess annealing time would cause grain growth that erases the heterogeneous gradient.
Phase-selective recrystallization has improved strength and ductility in a Ni-Co-Cr-Fe-Al-W eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The specific response of AlCoCrFeNi to the proposed partial-recrystallization treatment is not documented in the cited evidence.
HIP at 1100 °C and 100 MPa for 2 hours will eliminate defects and homogenize AlCoCrFeNi without creating a heterogeneous grain structure.
The effectiveness of the back-stress mechanism depends on the volume fraction and size distribution of ultrafine grains.
